settings.advanced.title: Advanced
settings.advanced.desc: Expert-only knobs for SMART scan controls (wake Drives, max-age safety net), Docker container visibility, and more. Defaults are safe — only change these if you understand the trade-offs.
settings.advanced.smart.title: SMART scan controls
settings.advanced.smart.wake_desc: By default, NAS Doctor skips drives that are in standby — SMART history will show gaps when drives are sleeping, and that's intentional (reduces wear). Enabling this option forces smartctl to wake spun-down drives on every scan cycle. At the default 30-min scan interval, that's roughly 48 extra spin-ups per drive per day. Only enable if your drives never spin down, or if you deliberately need every-cycle SMART monitoring and accept the wear cost.
settings.advanced.smart.max_age.label: Max days without SMART read
settings.advanced.smart.max_age.desc: If a drive stays in standby longer than this many days without a successful SMART read, NAS Doctor will force one wake-up to refresh SMART data. Lower values keep SMART data fresher at the cost of more spin-ups; higher values reduce wear but let drives go longer unobserved. Set to 0 to disable the safety net entirely — SMART will never force a wake-up (v0.9.5 behaviour). Valid range 0–30.
settings.advanced.intervals.title: Per-subsystem scan intervals
settings.advanced.intervals.desc: Override the global scan cadence per subsystem. Use Use global to inherit the Diagnostic Scan Interval (most users want this). Set a positive interval only if you want that subsystem to run faster or slower than the rest of the dashboard. Values persist immediately, but no scheduler behaviour changes until the slice-2b release.
settings.advanced.docker_hide.title: Hide Docker containers from dashboard
settings.advanced.docker_hide.desc: Tick the containers you want hidden from the Docker Containers section. Stats history is still collected and alerts still fire — the containers are hidden from the tile, not suppressed. Top Processes container attribution is not affected: if a hidden container is chewing CPU you'll still see its name there.
settings.advanced.borg.title: Backup Monitors → Borg
settings.advanced.borg.desc: Monitor externally-managed BorgBackup repos (e.g. Unraid User Scripts setups) by bind-mounting the repo path into the NAS Doctor container. The borg binary is bundled in the image; you only need to mount the repo. Set BORG_PASSPHRASE in Docker env vars for encrypted repos.
settings.advanced.duplicacy.title: Backup Monitors → Duplicacy
settings.advanced.duplicacy.desc: Monitor Duplicacy backups by bind-mounting either the repo root (CLI install) or the cache directory (saspus/duplicacy-web) into NAS Doctor. Disk-read only — the duplicacy binary is never invoked. Pick CLI repo for vanilla installs (path is the repo root); pick Web cache for duplicacy-web (path is the cache root, plus the per-repo storage id).
